# Third-party notices

## Design reference

Indus Agent's design is inspired by **hermes-agent** by Nous Research
(<https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent>), released under the MIT License. We studied its
behaviour at commit `ab3fe9dffb0a89d534cb795e2a2940e5f6542056`.

Indus Agent is written from scratch. No source code, comments, documentation, tests or assets of
hermes-agent are included in this repository. The clean-room guards in `tooling/checks/` (similarity,
banned identifiers, asset hashes) check every change against the pinned reference, in CI and before
each release; the protocol is described in `docs/plan/01-clean-room-protocol.md`.

We include the reference's licence below as credit:

```text
MIT License

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal
in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights

copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is

The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
copies or substantial portions of the Software.

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR

SOFTWARE.
```

## What Indus Agent ships

Every component below is redistributed by at least one way of installing Indus Agent (installers, Docker image, desktop app, `uv sync` with extras): 167 Python packages, 262 npm packages bundled into the dashboard, terminal UI and desktop app, 5 pinned binaries and 1 base image. "Used by" says which part brings each one in: `base` is the core install, `extra <name>` an optional extra, `apps/<name>` a JavaScript app.

Components are grouped by licence (SPDX expression). Each licence's full text follows once at the end; every package's own copyright notice stays in its distribution.

## Obligations

- **GPL-2.0-only**: Git for Windows is redistributed unmodified as the upstream PortableGit archive. Its corresponding source is published by the Git for Windows project for the same version tag; on request we provide the source for the exact build we pin (written offer, valid three years from the release that ships it).
- **LGPL-2.1-or-later**: the FFmpeg libraries inside the `av` wheels and alsa-lib (libasound) inside the `sherpa-onnx` Linux wheels are separate shared libraries that a user can replace; their source is available from the FFmpeg and ALSA projects and the PyAV and sherpa-onnx releases that built them. We do not modify them.
- **MPL-2.0**: file-level copyleft. We ship MPL-2.0 packages unmodified; their source is available from the package index. If we ever change an MPL-2.0 file, the changed file stays MPL-2.0 and its source must be published.

## Build tools (never shipped)

`electron-builder` (MIT) is a development dependency of `apps/desktop` that turns the staged app into installers (P20-38); nothing of it is copied into the packaged app (`apps/desktop/scripts/stage-app.mjs` stages only production packages and refuses any licence that is not on the allow-list). Its tree contains packages under licences outside our allow-list; the licence guard gates production dependencies only, so they are recorded here while the owner's ruling on build-only licences is pending (D-16.715). Other CI-only tools (hadolint, GPL-3.0; actionlint, MIT) run in CI and are never shipped.
